title: perf(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions and enforce rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds automatic performance regression detection for canaries with hysteresis and rollout guard integration; default thresholds are conservative and configurable via perf_canary config; rollout will auto-pause and shift traffic back on confirmed regressions.
body: Context: we need continuous perf monitoring that can automatically detect significant latency/throughput regressions during canary rollouts and prevent bad model/config rollouts from impacting production. This PR implements an autodetect pipeline that computes rolling stats (P50/P95/P99 and throughput) per-route and per-model, applies an adaptive threshold with hysteresis to avoid flapping, and integrates directly with the rollout controller to pause and rollback traffic when a regression is confirmed. What changed: 1) perf-canary/detector.py: new detector that ingests aggregated metrics, runs a bootstrap t-test + nonparametric shift detection for latency and throughput, and produces an alert token with confidence and suggested action; 2) perf-canary/hysteresis.py: reusable hysteresis utilities to require sustained violations over a configurable window before triggering; 3) perf-canary/rollout_guard.py: integrates detector outputs with the rollout state machine to auto-pause rollouts and optionally shift traffic back to the previous model variant; 4) observability/metrics.yaml: new perf canary metrics (perf_canary_detects_total, perf_canary_confirmed_regressions_total, perf_canary_hysteresis_state) and dashboards updated; 5) perf-canary/tests/test_autodetect.py: unit and e2e style tests that run synthetic traces to validate detection sensitivity and hysteresis; 6) infra/ci/perf-workflow.yml: new perf CI job that runs the lightweight canary e2e on PRs touching runtime or perf-canary code; 7) docs/perf-canary.md: documentation describing detection algorithm, config knobs, and operational runbook. Defaults: conservative thresholds (5% P95 increase sustained for 3 windows, 95% CI) and KV-cache-aware comparisons to avoid false positives during cold-cache events. Feature flag: perf_canary_autodetect_v2 gate is added so rollout rollout teams can opt-in. Tests: added unit tests for statistical detector, synthetic e2e that simulates a throughput regression and verifies auto-pause and traffic shift. CI: perf-e2e initially flaked due to timing on GH runners, increased timeouts and re-ran; all checks now pass. Why this approach: we observed manual canary reviews missing regressions that only show up under specific sequence-length distributions and cache hit patterns; automatic detection with hysteresis and direct rollout integration reduces MTTI and prevents customer impact. Rollout guard behavior: on confirmed regression the rollout controller will: (a) mark canary as paused, (b) emit a structured alert to Ops with diagnostics (route, model id, metric deltas, confidence), (c) automatically shift remaining canary traffic back to the previous stable variant if allowed by config, (d) keep the canary state for easy repro and manual inspection. Backwards compatible: the detector runs async and does not change default rollout behavior until the feature flag is enabled. Migration/ops: added a short runbook in docs/perf-canary.md describing tuning thresholds, how to opt in, and how to acknowledge/override an auto-pause. Related: ENG-13245 (perf canary roadmap), ENG-13300 (rollout controller integrations), PM-44 (product acceptance criteria).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can we reduce false positives from cache churn? Please ensure detector compares cache-aware baselines or tags cold-cache windows.
Author (Asha): Added KV-cache-aware baseline and an exclusion rule for obvious cold-cache spikes; referenced ENG-13300 for further followups.
Riley Chen: The 3-window hysteresis feels arbitrary; can we make it configurable and document recommended values?
Author (Asha): Made window_count configurable via perf_canary.hysteresis.window_count and added guidance in docs with recommended defaults.
Samir Gupta: CI perf-e2e flaked in initial run — please increase timeouts and add deterministic fixtures.
Author (Asha): Increased perf job timeout to 25m, added deterministic synthetic trace generator; reran and verified green.
Riley Chen: Approving after doc updates and adding a small e2e to validate rollback path.
Miguel Torres: Approved — good to merge once CI is green.
merge_commit_message: perf(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions and enforce rollout guards\n\nAdds autodetect pipeline, hysteresis utilities, rollout guard integration, perf CI job, tests and docs.
notes: Operational impact: reduces time-to-detect regressions and prevents bad rollouts from completing; operators should start with conservative thresholds and tune per-service.
Monitoring: new dashboards added under Observability > Performance Canary; alerts published to #perf-canary on Slack.
Follow-ups: ENG-13450 to add ML-based anomaly model; ENG-13451 to surface suggested remediation steps in the Console.
